title: Finite evaluation and bounded site transport of the Brown tower adjoint
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p$, and a $k$-morphism $f:X\to Y$ between separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, valuation ring $R$, uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Choose a compactification $c=(X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{g}Y)$, with $j$ open and $g$ proper [def-weil-compactifications-refinements].

For $T=X,\overline X,Y$, let $\mathsf S_T^{\mathrm{et}}$ and $\mathsf S_T^{\mathrm{proet}}$ be the abelian categories of strict systems of $(A_n)_T$-module sheaves on the indicated small sites, with semilinear quotient transitions and componentwise exactness; use their ordinary unbounded derived categories and exact evaluations $e_n$ [lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison]. Put $F^{\mathrm{et}}=Rg_{*,\bullet}^{\mathrm{et}}j_{!,\bullet}^{\mathrm{et}}$ and $F_n^{\mathrm{et}}=Rg_{*,n}^{\mathrm{et}}j_{!,n}^{\mathrm{et}}$. Choose the $R$-linear Brown adjunction $F^{\mathrm{et}}\dashv G^{\mathrm{et}}$ of [lem-pur-etale-tower-brown-adjunction]. Let $f_n^\times$ be the ordinary unbounded etale right adjoint of $F_n^{\mathrm{et}}$ [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. Let $LE_n^T\dashv e_n$ be the derived extension from one level [lem-pur-coefficient-evaluation-derived-left-adjoint], so $e_q LE_n^T P=P\otimes^L_{A_n}A_q$ for $q\le n$ and is zero for $q>n$. The natural transformation
$$\chi_n:LE_n^YF_n^{\mathrm{et}}\longrightarrow F^{\mathrm{et}}LE_n^X$$
whose evaluation-adjunction transpose is the identity is invertible on all objects. For every etale derived system $Q$ there are natural isomorphisms $e_nG^{\mathrm{et}}Q\cong f_n^\times(e_nQ)$. They identify evaluated counits with finite counits. The actual transition adjoint of $G^{\mathrm{et}}Q$ from level $m$ to level $n$ is the transpose of the coefficient-extended finite counit followed by the transition of $Q$; these are the ordinary exceptional coefficient mates and obey the quotient cocycle, as equalities of actual transformations of systems.

Let $C$ be a bounded-below normalized pro-etale derived system of etale origin, with finite bounded constructible finite-Tor evaluations. Write $\nu_{T,\bullet}^*\dashv R\nu_{T,\bullet,*}$ for the ordinary system site adjunction and put $Q=R\nu_{Y,\bullet,*}C$. Suppose the finite exceptional images $Rf_n^!C_n$ have a common lower cohomological bound. Here $Rf_n^!$ is the finite etale-origin adjoint transported as in [lem-pur-finite-coefficient-adjoint-comparisons]. Then $G^{\mathrm{et}}Q$ is bounded below and
$$N=\nu_{X,\bullet}^*G^{\mathrm{et}}Q$$
is a bounded-below normalized pro-etale derived system, with canonical counit-preserving isomorphisms $N_n\cong Rf_n^!C_n$ and the specified finite coefficient-mate transitions. There is an actual transported tower counit $FN\to C$. For every bounded-below pro-etale derived system $B$ of etale origin, the transported Brown bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(B,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(FB,C)$ is natural and $R$-linear. Site comparison is fully faithful on these bounded-below systems, including morphisms. No right adjoint on all unbounded pro-etale complexes is asserted.

source.place: Agent ordinary-derived refinement of the tower adjunction used in the first Hom display; returned item proof Steps 4–5, using derived left adjoints to evaluation and bounded-below site comparison.

proof.text: Choose the finite-evaluation package and the compatible geometric comparisons before transporting any counit or Hom bijection.

The evaluated exceptional comparison is the explicit paste of site inverse evaluation, Brown finite evaluation and site direct evaluation. Bounded site units give bijectivity on Hom by the adjunction Hom equivalence. Exact open extension preserves each lower bound, and the right adjoint of exact proper pullback preserves each lower bound too.

At C with common finite exceptional lower bound, the geometric bound makes G(V_Y C) bounded below. Invert d at that object and compose V_Y.inverse of the Brown counit with the Y site counit. This explicitly defines the transported counit, and cancellation of d proves its pinned equation.

Compose the X site-counit Hom congruence, inverse of full faithfulness of X inverse image, inverse of the Brown adjunction Hom equivalence, inverse of the Y site Hom equivalence, and compact-support comparison Hom congruence. Naturality of d proves that this equivalence sends a to P.map a followed by the constructed counit. Brown compatibility follows by the same naturality square. Naturality in both variables follows from functoriality and naturality of the Brown and site counits.

The exact-derived factorization identifies each derived inverse image with the standard exact-derived functor and hence makes it additive. Adjunction makes proper direct image additive, so P is additive and the Hom bijection preserves sums. Brown right-linearity and naturality of d and of its counit give the specified scalar equation. Assemble TransportData and Transport from these explicit constructions.
